Camila — thanks again for the demo today. Hypha is evaluating a platform to power our patient outreach summaries and in particular we need price certainty for budgeting across our multi-year grant cycle.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a fixed unit price for 3 years (we'd like a hard anchor) or an explicit uplift cap per year?
- Can you include a renewal-protection clause so we are not subject to >5% annual increases without notice?

If you can send a high-level term sheet with those elements we can prioritize this with finance.

Best,

VP Product, Hypha Health

Maya — great to hear. Attached is a draft SOW + a model showing a 3-year fixed unit price option and an alternative with a 3% uplift cap. High-level:

Option A — 3-year fixed anchor
- Fixed per-token equivalent price for 36 months
- Annual review limited to currency / compliance-driven fees only
- Early-termination: standard pro-rata + 60d notice

Option B — 3-year capped uplift
- Starting price lower than A (year 1) with an annual cap at +3%
- Renewal protection: if market rates drop, Hypha may opt into lower public pricing at renewal

We typically require exec sign-off for multi-year price anchoring or any commitment with below-market protection. Ben, can you weigh in on margin impact? If this looks viable I'll route to Legal for a narrow renewal-protection clause and then request exec approval.

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Hypha_SOW_v2.pdf, hypha_price_model_3yr.xlsx

Subject: Re: Exec sign-off request: 3-year fixed-price anchoring + renewal protection (Hypha Health)

Quick margin note — ran the model. Summary:
- Option A (fixed anchor) reduces expected gross margin by ~17% over baseline list across three years, mostly concentrated in year 2–3 if volumes ramp faster than forecast.
- Option B (3% uplift cap) keeps blended margin only ~6% below target and preserves upside if volume exceeds the conservative forecast.

Recommendation: pursue Option B with a limited renewal-protection clause that prevents >5% automatic increases but preserves the right for Redwood to propose alternate commercial terms at renewal if materially different capacity/throughput is required.

If execs want stronger customer guarantees (i.e., fixed anchor), we'll need a revenue commitment band or an elevated per-token floor.

Ben Carter
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — read the memo and model. Decision: Approve Option B (3% uplift cap) with the following executive conditions:

1) Add a 12-month minimum spend band tied to a reduced per-token floor. If Hypha misses >50% of committed spend after 12 months, Redwood may convert remaining term to list-based pricing with a 90d notice.
2) Renewal-protection: contract may not be increased >5% annually without mutual written agreement; exception clauses for regulatory/compliance cost pass-throughs only.
3) Legal to use the redlined paragraph below for the renewal-protection clause; commercial to confirm final numbers before signature.

Redlined renewal-protection (for Legal):
"Redwood shall not increase the per-unit price by more than five percent (5%) in any consecutive 12-month period during the initial term and any automatic renewal, except for taxes, regulatory fees, or material changes in underlying infrastructure costs documented in writing and mutually agreed."

Camila — please confirm Hypha accepts these conditions in principle and flag any procurement/legal asks. Ben/Legal, route final SOW and DocuSign link when ready.

-Aditya Rao
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
